about.p1: Most people arrive here having been burned once already — a developer who went quiet, or an agency that took the budget and assigned a junior who relearns the project every week. Watad was founded in 2025 by engineers who had already spent years shipping production systems in healthcare, e-commerce, and fintech. That experience is why the first thing we give you is a written scope, and why nothing we build stops at a demo.
about.p2: You talk directly to the people building your product — no account manager relaying your words into a ticket. Designer and engineer working side by side, which is why decisions take hours instead of weeks. Browse

faq.intro: Short, direct answers — the same ones you'd get on a call, without booking one.

items.question: What does Watad do?
items.answer: Watad builds custom web applications, mobile apps, and workflow automation for founders and operating businesses — primarily across Jordan and the wider MENA region. Every engagement starts with a written scope and ends with a full handover, not just a demo.

items.question: Who is Watad for?
items.answer: Founders launching a new product, and operators running an existing business who need software built and properly handed over — with documentation and access, not held together by a team you can't reach afterward.

items.question: Where is Watad based, and which regions do you work with?
items.answer: Watad is based in Amman, Jordan, and works primarily with founders and businesses across Jordan and the MENA region, though the team also takes on projects outside the region.

items.question: How long does a typical project take?
items.answer: Most engagements run the full process — discovery, design, development, and launch — in about a month, depending on project size. You get a demo every week, so you always know where things stand.

items.question: What's included when a project is handed over?
items.answer: A production deploy, technical documentation, full credentials, and a walkthrough session — enough for your own team to run and extend the system without calling us for small things.

items.question: What technologies does Watad use?
items.answer: The stack is chosen per project rather than fixed — commonly ASP.NET Core, React and React Native, cloud hosting on AWS or Azure, and n8n for workflow automation, picked for what the product actually needs.

items.question: How much does a project cost?
items.answer: Pricing is scoped per project after a discovery call. Watad avoids fixed package pricing because a marketing site, an MVP, and a multi-tenant platform don't cost the same to build properly.

items.question: How do I start a project with Watad?
items.answer: Book a 30-minute call or send project details through the contact form. You'll get a reply within 24 hours — including if Watad isn't the right fit for it.

process.intro: Four phases — the full process typically lands in one month, and the exact timeline depends on the project size. Every week you know exactly where things stand and what comes next.
process.metric1Label: Full process — depends on project size

steps.title: Discovery
steps.description: We agree on goals, users, constraints, and what success will be measured by — before any code exists. Changing your mind on paper costs a conversation; changing it in code costs a sprint.

steps.title: Design
steps.description: You see and click through the product before it's built. Wireframes, then screens, then a working prototype your team reviews — so ideas change in Figma rather than in production.

steps.title: Development
steps.description: Iterative builds with something tangible to look at every week — APIs, frontend or app, and automated checks running from the start. Nothing is saved up for a single delivery-day reveal.

steps.title: Launch
steps.description: We launch alongside you, stabilise alongside you, and hand over properly — documentation, credentials, and a walkthrough — until your team can run the system without calling us for small things.
